items.title: Clay Jenkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 18, 2016
items.q: I have a neat thing with Clark Terry and Joe Williams talking about THE blue notes.

ctx.x: That’s right. Guitars. You better be. I make my students, you know we play the blues in every key every day, just on your own with a metronome. Be able to play what you’re hearing and make — and it’s also, you know — when I was younger I would play — I was okay, but I didn’t make that statement like what we call kind of the A-A-B or the consequent phrase. Like so many blues songs, “I left my baby and don’t know what to do” with a period there. And then for a chance for the listener to absorb it. And the next four…
I have a neat thing with Clark Terry and Joe Williams talking about THE blue notes.

Yeah. Those worried notes. Oh yeah. Well that’s all in the gesture too. And the nuance. Yeah. And those guys and the Delta guys, they didn’t know the third and the flatted third and all that. So it was nuanced. It was worrying that stuff. That’s the way a friend of mine described it. Worrying the third, worrying the fifth. Yeah. It’s really important.
